Symlink `br` -> `bf` for backward compatibility. No daemon, no systemd unit — each `bf` invocation is self-contained.\n1250\t\n1251\t---\n1252\t\n1253\t## Phase 7: Upstream Robustness Parity (br backports)\n1254\t\n1255\tUpstream `beads_rust` has kept shipping at remarkable velocity since the fork (reference:\n1256\t`Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust` `main` @ `8bff67a`, 2026-07-21 — nearly 400 issues worked,\n1257\tmost of them hardening the exact dual-store failure modes bf has hit in production). This\n1258\tphase ports the **robustness behaviors** into bf's architecture. Concepts only, not code —\n1259\tthe codebases have diverged too far to merge, upstream accepts no PRs (one-way flow), and\n1260\tattribution is carried here (beads_rust is MIT). Product-surface breadth is explicitly out\n1261\tof scope (see Non-goals).\n1262\t\n1263\tItems are ordered P0 → P2. Each maps to a standing bf pain point documented in incident\n1264\tmemory or CLAUDE.md.\n1265\t\n1266\t### 7.1 Incremental auto-flush + dirty tracking (P0) — amends Core Principle 2\n1267\t\n1268\tThe single highest-value port. Upstream writes the JSONL after every successful mutation;\n1269\tbf's flush-on-demand model is why db-only beads exist and why CLAUDE.md carries the\n1270\t\"ALWAYS `bf sync --flush-only` before repair\" ritual (post-2026-06-10 wipe).\n1271\t\n1272\t- New `dirty_issues` table (`issue_id`, `marked_at`); every mutation marks its issue dirty.\n1273\t- After each successful mutation: best-effort incremental export of *dirty rows only* into\n1274\t  the JSONL (surgical line replacement, not full rewrite). On failure: warn loudly (stderr\n1275\t  + `warning` field in the `--json` envelope), keep the dirty marks, never fail the\n1276\t  mutation. Named recovery: `bf sync --flush-only`.\n1277\t- Config `sync.auto_flush` (default **true**); `--no-auto-flush` per-invocation override.\n1278\t- `bf batch` flushes once at transaction end, not per-op (write amplification).\n1279\t- Read-only and diagnostic commands never write the JSONL (upstream's #326 lesson:\n1280\t  status/doctor commands that rewrite the artifact create git churn and mask real drift).\n1281\t\n1282\t**Exit criteria:** the flush-before-repair ritual is deletable from CLAUDE.md; killing a\n1283\tworker at any point between mutation and flush loses nothing that `git diff .beads/` can't\n1284\tshow; flush failure is visible in machine-readable output.\n1285\t\n1286\t### 7.2 Doctor safety stack (P0)\n1287\t\n1288\tbf's current guard (refuse/flush-first before repair) is one check. Upstream's is a layered\n1289\tarchitecture; port the layers:\n1290\t\n1291\t1. **Healthy early-return** — `bf doctor --repair` on a workspace with no errors runs only\n1292\t   trivial fixers and exits; it must be provably impossible to reach the JSONL rebuild from\n1293\t   a healthy state.\n1294\t2. **Local repair first** — integrity-check triage, VACUUM/REINDEX, cache rebuilds. The\n1295\t   JSONL rebuild is the last resort, not the first tool.\n1296\t3. **Verified pre-rebuild backups** — SHA-256-hashed copies of the full DB family into a\n1297\t   recovery dir before any rebuild; restore-on-failure; `bf doctor runs` / `bf doctor\n1298\t   restore <run-id|latest>` to list and roll back.\n1299\t4. **JSONL authority preflight** — refuse rebuild if the JSONL contains merge-conflict\n1300\t   markers or invalid records (rebuilding from a poisoned authority is how a bad flush\n1301\t   becomes permanent).\n1302\t5. **Repeat-failure refusal** — a rebuild whose post-verification failed writes a marker;\n1303\t   further rebuilds refuse without `--allow-repeated-repair`.\n1304\t6. **Preservation across rebuild** — snapshot unflushed **dirty issues** (with labels,\n1305\t   dependencies, comments) *and* tombstones before rebuild; restore and re-mark dirty\n1306\t   after; report the count in the repair summary. This is `beads_rust#394` (filed by us\n1307\t   upstream 2026-07-21) — implement it here first.\n1308\t\n1309\t**Exit criteria:** an induced rebuild on a workspace with unflushed beads loses nothing;\n1310\trepair on a healthy workspace is a no-op; every rebuild leaves a restorable, hash-verified\n1311\tbackup.\n1312\t\n1313\t### 7.3 NULL-datetime & schema hardening (P0, small)\n1314\t\n1315\tFix the `parse_datetime` crash on NULL datetime columns (the flush/list crash class that\n1316\tpreviously forced the destructive `rm beads.db + reimport` workaround). Add a doctor\n1317\tdetector + repair fixer for NULL-in-NOT-NULL rows generally.\n1318\t\n1319\t### 7.4 Anomaly classification & sync verdicts (P1)\n1320\t\n1321\t- An `AnomalyClass` enum with severity tiers: `DbNewer`, `JsonlNewer`, `CountMismatch`,\n1322\t  `IdSetMismatch`, `ConflictMarkers`, `DatabaseCorrupt`, … surfaced uniformly in\n1323\t  `bf doctor --json`.\n1324\t- `bf sync --status` renders an **\"In sync\" verdict** backed by evidence: stored\n1325\t  `jsonl_content_hash` matches computed hash AND `dirty_issues` is empty.\n1326\t\n1327\t**Exit criteria:** the manual corruption-triage ritual (compare `git log -1 issues.jsonl`\n1328\tagainst bead counts) is replaced by one command with a machine-readable verdict.\n1329\t\n1330\t### 7.5 `update` description editing (P1)\n1331\t\n1332\t`bf update --description` / `--description-file` / `--acceptance-criteria` — closes the\n1333\tdocumented \"bf update cannot edit description; add a comment instead\" gap. Lesson from\n1334\tupstream's #386 regression: the fix must be wired through the real update path and covered\n1335\tby a round-trip integration test (their first fix for this shipped without ever touching\n1336\t`update.rs`).\n1337\t\n1338\t### 7.6 Batch surface expansion (P1)\n1339\t\n1340\t`bf batch` today supports only create/dep_add_blocker/close. Expand to a uniform op set\n1341\t(update, label add/remove, dep add/remove, comment) inside one transaction with one\n1342\tauto-flush at the end. The bf-5id blocked→open cascade must hold identically in the batch\n1343\tclose path.\n1344\t\n1345\t### 7.7 JSON contract discipline (P1)\n1346\t\n1347\t- One stable envelope shape for every command's `--json` output — fixes the\n1348\t  `bf ready` (JSON array) vs `bf list` (NDJSON) divergence that silently miscounts under\n1349\t  `json.load`.\n1350\t- `bf robot-docs`: machine-readable enumeration of every command's contract, for agent\n1351\t  consumers (NEEDLE worker prompts reference it instead of hardcoding shapes).\n1352\t\n1353\t### 7.8 Derived blocked status (P2 — architectural)\n1354\t\n1355\tUpstream computes blocked-ness from the dependency graph (with a `blocked_issues_cache`\n1356\tinvalidated on dep/close mutations) instead of storing a status that must be transitioned.\n1357\tThis deletes the bf-5id bug class (stuck-blocked beads stalling workers) at the root — the\n1358\tjust-shipped cascade fix treats the symptom.\n1359\t\n1360\t**Hard constraint:** NEEDLE's safe-dispatch fences beads by manually setting\n1361\t`status=blocked`. A derived model MUST retain an explicit manual hold that presents as\n1362\tblocked and takes precedence over the derived value (dedicated flag or a preserved manual\n1363\tstatus — decide at design time, with NEEDLE-side review). CLI and JSONL compatibility:\n1364\tconsumers keep seeing `status: \"blocked\"`.\n1365\t\n1366\tIncludes a migration for existing stored-blocked rows.\n1367\t\n1368\t### 7.9 Multi-box & fleet concurrency (P2)\n1369\t\n1370\t- **Merge anchor** (`beads.base.jsonl`): a base snapshot enabling 3-way merge of JSONL\n1371\t  across checkouts — targets the recurring lab/ex44 divergence.\n1372\t- **Concurrent-writer hardening**: fleet-scale tests (N concurrent `bf` processes doing\n1373\t  create/claim/close) hunting the upstream-documented classes — parallel-write silent loss,\n1374\t  spurious sync conflicts during auto-import.\n1375\t- **Pre-export history backups** (`.bf_history/` with prune policy): one more insurance\n1376\t  layer under the JSONL, cheap to keep.\n1377\t\n1378\t### Non-goals\n1379\t\n1380\tUpstream surface deliberately NOT ported: the MCP server, workflow gates /\n1381\ttransition-scoped required fields, scheduler, agent-coordination module, epic containment,\n1382\tcapacity/admission control, and graph-analytics TUI. NEEDLE owns orchestration in this\n1383\tstack; `bv` exists for visualization; bf's identity is the lean, fleet-hardened store.\n1384\tPreserve bf's own differentiators upstream lacks: atomic `claim`, `critical_path`,\n1385\t`velocity`, `commit_check`, secret scanning, genesis beads, annotations.\n1386\t\n1387\t### Open questions\n1388\t\n1389\t- Auto-flush × rotation: incremental flush must target only the active `issues.jsonl`,\n1390\t  never archives — confirm rotation interplay before 7.1 ships.\n1391\t- Does auto-flush change git-commit cadence guidance for NEEDLE workers (`.beads/` will now\n1392\t  be dirty far more often between commits)?\n1393\t- 7.8 manual-hold representation (new flag vs preserved manual status) needs NEEDLE-side\n1394\t  review before implementation — do not start 7.8 until that decision is recorded here.\n1395\t\n1396\t---\n1397\t\n1398\t## Test Strategy & Isolation\n1399\t\n1400\tbf must be testable without touching, modifying, or interfering with any live `br` workspace. Three isolation concerns drive the test strategy:\n1401\t\n1402\t### Rule 1: Never Share a Live Database\n1403\t\n1404\tbf tests **never** auto-discover or open a `.beads/beads.db` that `br` is actively using. SQLite WAL mode serializes writers, so concurrent opens are safe from a corruption standpoint — but test mutations (creates, claims, closes) would contaminate real workspaces with spurious beads.\n1405\t\n1406\tAll tests target exactly one of:\n1407\t- **`:memory:`** — rusqlite in-memory database (unit tests, zero disk I/O)\n1408\t- **`tempfile::tempdir()`** — ephemeral directory deleted on drop (integration tests)\n1409\t- **Read-only fixture copy** — `issues.jsonl` copied out of a real workspace into a tempdir, never written back (compat tests)\n1410\t\n1411\t### Rule 2: Never Point `br` at a bf Test Database\n1412\t\n1413\tThe schema compat test must verify `br` can read a `bf`-created database — but it cannot use br's own workspace for this. The test creates a fresh tempdir, runs `bf init` + `bf create` in it, then invokes `br --db /path/to/temp/beads.db` against that file. The real `br` workspace is untouched.\n1414\t\n1415\t### Rule 3: JSONL Fixture = Read-Only Copy\n1416\t\n1417\tThe JSONL round-trip test uses a snapshot of a real workspace's `issues.jsonl` as a fixture, not a live file. The fixture is checked into `tests/fixtures/` (or copied at test time with `--allow-stale`). `bf sync --import` loads it into a tempdir database; `bf list --format json` is compared against the expected output derived from `br list --format json` run against the same snapshot.\n1418\t\n1419\t```\n1420\ttests/fixtures/\n1421\t├── forge-snapshot.jsonl    # snapshot of FORGE workspace (committed, static)\n1422\t└── needle-snapshot.jsonl   # snapshot of NEEDLE workspace\n1423\t```\n1424\t\n1425\tThese fixtures are updated manually when the schema changes: `cp /home/coding/FORGE/.beads/issues.jsonl tests/fixtures/forge-snapshot.jsonl`.\n1426\t\n1427\t### Test Harness (`tests/common/mod.rs`)\n1428\t\n1429\t```rust\n1430\tpub struct TempWorkspace {\n1431\t    dir: tempfile::TempDir,   // deleted on drop — no cleanup needed\n1432\t    pub db_path: PathBuf,\n1433\t    pub storage: Storage,\n1434\t}\n1435\t\n1436\timpl TempWorkspace {\n1437\t    pub fn new() -> Result<Self> {\n1438\t        let dir = tempfile::tempdir()?;\n1439\t        let db_path = dir.path().join(\".beads/beads.db\");\n1440\t        fs::create_dir(dir.path().join(\".beads\"))?;\n1441\t        let storage = Storage::open(&db_path)?;\n1442\t        Ok(Self { dir, db_path, storage })\n1443\t    }\n1444\t\n1445\t    pub fn from_fixture(jsonl: &Path) -> Result<Self> {\n1446\t        let ws = Self::new()?;\n1447\t        import_jsonl(jsonl, &ws.storage)?;\n1448\t        Ok(ws)\n1449\t    }\n1450\t\n1451\t    // Run br against this workspace's db (for compat tests)\n1452\t    pub fn br(&self, args: &[&str]) -> std::process::Output {\n1453\t        Command::new(\"br\")\n1454\t            .arg(\"--db\").arg(&self.db_path)\n1455\t            .args(args)\n1456\t            .output()\n1457\t            .expect(\"br not in PATH\")\n1458\t    }\n1459\t}\n1460\t```\n1461\t\n1462\tUnit tests in `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `Storage::open(\":memory:\")` directly — no `TempWorkspace` needed.\n1463\t\n1464\t### Schema Forward-Compatibility\n1465\t\n1466\tbf adds tables that br doesn't know about. No columns are added to the shared `issues` table.\n1467\t\n1468\t| Addition | br behavior |\n1469\t|----------|-------------|\n1470\t| `bead_annotations` table | br ignores unknown tables entirely; `issues` column count is unchanged so `issues_column_order_matches()` passes and `rebuild_issues_table()` never fires |\n1471\t| `worker_sessions` table | Same — ignored |\n1472\t| `velocity_stats` table | Same — ignored |\n1473\t| `critical_path_cache` table | Same — ignored |\n1474\t\n1475\t**Why no column on `issues`**: br's `issues_column_order_matches()` in `schema.rs:630` checks `actual_columns.len() != EXPECTED_ISSUE_COLUMN_ORDER.len()`. Any extra column causes this to return `false`, which triggers `rebuild_issues_table()` — a full DROP + recreate using only br's canonical column list. An `annotations` column on `issues` would be silently destroyed on every `br` open. Storing annotations in `bead_annotations` sidesteps this entirely.\n1476\t\n1477\tMigration on `Storage::open` (fully idempotent — all `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`):\n1478\t\n1479\t```rust\n1480\tfn apply_migrations(conn: &Connection) -> Result<()> {\n1481\t    conn.execute_batch(\"\n1482\t        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bead_annotations (\n1483\t            bead_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES issues(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n1484\t            key     TEXT NOT NULL,\n1485\t            value   TEXT NOT NULL,\n1486\t            PRIMARY KEY (bead_id, key)\n1487\t        );\n1488\t        CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bead_annotations_key_value\n1489\t            ON bead_annotations (key, value);\n1490\t        -- other bf-only tables follow\n1491\t    \")?;\n1492\t    Ok(())\n1493\t}\n1494\t```\n1495\t\n1496\tNo `ALTER TABLE` on `issues`, ever. The migration is a pure table-creation pass.\n1497\t\n1498\t---\n1499\t\n1500\t## Compatibility Verification\n1501\t\n1502\tAll tests run against **isolated temp workspaces** — no live br workspace is touched.\n1503\t\n1504\t### JSONL Round-Trip Test\n1505\t\n1506\t```bash\n1507\t# 1. Copy real workspace JSONL as a read-only fixture (never modify the original)\n1508\tFIXTURE=$(mktemp -d)\n1509\tcp /home/coding/FORGE/.beads/issues.jsonl \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\"\n1510\t\n1511\t# 2. bf imports the fixture into a fresh tempdir\n1512\tBFDIR=$(mktemp -d)\n1513\tbf init --prefix fg --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1514\tbf sync --import-only --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" --jsonl \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\"\n1515\t\n1516\t# 3. bf exports its view of the data\n1517\tbf list --format json --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" | jq -S '.' > /tmp/bf-output.jsonl\n1518\t\n1519\t# 4. br reads the original JSONL directly (read-only, not our tempdir)\n1520\tbr list --format json --db \"$FIXTURE/issues.jsonl\" --no-db | jq -S '.' > /tmp/br-output.jsonl\n1521\t\n1522\t# 5. Compare (order-independent by ID)\n1523\tdiff /tmp/bf-output.jsonl /tmp/br-output.jsonl\n1524\t# Must be empty — bf and br produce identical output from the same JSONL\n1525\t\n1526\t# Cleanup\n1527\trm -rf \"$FIXTURE\" \"$BFDIR\"\n1528\t```\n1529\t\n1530\t### Schema Forward-Compatibility Test\n1531\t\n1532\t```bash\n1533\t# 1. bf creates a workspace in a fresh tempdir (bf schema, including bf-only tables)\n1534\tBFDIR=$(mktemp -d)\n1535\tbf init --prefix fg --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1536\tbf create --title \"compat test\" --type task --priority 1 --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1537\tbf create --title \"another bead\" --type bug --priority 0 --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1538\tbf annotate fg-xxx needle_attempt=1 --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"\n1539\t# Annotation is stored in bead_annotations table, NOT in issues column\n1540\t\n1541\t# 2. br opens the same file (not its own workspace — pointed explicitly at the temp db)\n1542\tbr list --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"         # must list 2 beads without error\n1543\tbr doctor --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"       # must pass integrity check\n1544\t# Key assertion: br's issues_column_order_matches() sees exact column count → passes\n1545\t# rebuild_issues_table() is NOT triggered → bead_annotations table untouched\n1546\tbr update fg-xxx --status closed --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\"  # must succeed\n1547\t\n1548\t# 3. bf re-reads the br-mutated database (bead_annotations must survive br's UPDATE)\n1549\tbf show fg-xxx --db \"$BFDIR/beads.db\" --json | jq '.annotations'\n1550\t# Must still contain {\"needle_attempt\": \"1\"} — annotation row in bead_annotations\n1551\t# is untouched by br's UPDATE to the issues table\n1552\t\n1553\t# Cleanup\n1554\trm -rf \"$BFDIR\"\n1555\t```\n1556\t\n1557\t### Reverse Compatibility Test\n1558\t\n1559\t```bash\n1560\t# 1. br creates a workspace (br schema — no bead_annotations table, no velocity_stats table)\n1561\tBRDIR=$(mktemp -d)\n1562\tbr init --prefix fg --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"\n1563\tbr create \"br-created bead\" --type task --priority 2 --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"\n1564\t\n1565\t# 2. bf opens the br-created database\n1566\t# Storage::open runs apply_migrations() which creates bead_annotations + other bf-only\n1567\t# tables via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. No ALTER TABLE on issues is needed.\n1568\tbf list --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"         # must list the br-created bead without error\n1569\tbf annotate fg-yyy test_key=hello --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"  # inserts into bead_annotations\n1570\tbf show fg-yyy --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\" --json | jq '.annotations'\n1571\t# Must contain {\"test_key\": \"hello\"} — fetched via JOIN on bead_annotations\n1572\t\n1573\t# 3. br can still read the migrated database (new tables are ignored by br)\n1574\t# Critical: issues table column count is still exactly what br expects\n1575\tbr list --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"         # must still work\n1576\tbr doctor --db \"$BRDIR/beads.db\"       # must still pass — no issues column changes\n1577\t\n1578\t# Cleanup\n1579\trm -rf \"$BRDIR\"\n1580\t```\n1581\t\n1582\t### Claim Race Test\n1583\t\n1584\t```bash\n1585\t# Setup: create a test workspace with 10 beads of varying priority\n1586\tcd /tmp && rm -rf bf-test && mkdir bf-test && cd bf-test && bf init --prefix bf\n1587\tfor i in $(seq 1 10); do\n1588\t  bf create --title \"test-$i\" --priority $((i % 5))\n1589\tdone\n1590\t\n1591\t# === Test 1: Basic thundering herd (20 workers, 10 beads) ===\n1592\t# 20 workers claim simultaneously. Exactly 10 get a bead, 10 get NONE.\n1593\tfor i in $(seq 1 20); do\n1594\t  bf claim --any --assignee \"worker-$i\" --json > /tmp/claim-$i.out 2>&1 &\n1595\tdone\n1596\twait\n1597\t\n1598\t# Verify: exactly 10 claims succeeded, 10 returned NONE\n1599\tgrep -cl '\"id\"' /tmp/claim-*.out | wc -l  # must be 10\n1600\tgrep -cl 'NONE' /tmp/claim-*.out | wc -l  # must be 10\n1601\t\n1602\t# Verify: no bead claimed by more than one worker\n1603\tcat /tmp/claim-*.out | jq -r '.id' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn\n1604\t# Every ID must appear exactly once\n1605\t\n1606\t# === Test 2: Priority ordering ===\n1607\t# The 10 workers that succeeded should have beads in priority order\n1608\t# (priority 0 beads claimed before priority 4)\n1609\t# Verify by correlating claim output order with priority values\n1610\t\n1611\t# === Test 3: Sequential claims (depletion) ===\n1612\t# Create 20 more beads, claim one at a time, verify queue drains\n1613\tfor i in $(seq 11 30); do\n1614\t  bf create --title \"test-$i\" --priority $((i % 5))\n1615\tdone\n1616\tfor i in $(seq 1 20); do\n1617\t  result=$(bf claim --any --assignee \"seq-worker-$i\" --json)\n1618\t  [ -n \"$result\" ] && echo \"$result\" | jq -r '.id'\n1619\tdone\n1620\tbf list --status open --format json\n1621\t# Must return empty — all beads claimed\n1622\t\n1623\t# === Test 4: Stale claim reclamation ===\n1624\t# Claim a bead, manually age its updated_at past claim_ttl\n1625\t# Then claim again — the stale bead should be reclaimed and re-claimable\n1626\tbf claim --any --assignee \"dead-worker\" --json\n1627\t# (test harness: set claim_ttl to 5s for this test, or mock updated_at)\n1628\tbf doctor --reclaim-stale --ttl 0s\n1629\tbf list --status open --format json\n1630\t# The dead-worker's bead must be back in open status\n1631\t\n1632\t# === Test 5: Stale reclamation as side effect ===\n1633\t# Dead worker's bead is reclaimed when another worker claims\n1634\tbf claim --any --assignee \"scavenger\" --json\n1635\t# scavenger gets a bead; dead-worker's bead is also reclaimed to open\n1636\t\n1637\t# === Test 6: Multi-workspace claiming ===\n1638\t# Create two workspaces, claim --any gets highest priority across both\n1639\tmkdir /tmp/ws-a && cd /tmp/ws-a && bf init --prefix wa\n1640\tmkdir /tmp/ws-b && cd /tmp/ws-b && bf init --prefix wb\n1641\tbf create --title \"ws-a high\" --priority 0   # in ws-b\n1642\tbf create --title \"ws-a low\"  --priority 4   # in ws-b\n1643\tcd /tmp/ws-a && bf create --title \"ws-a mid\" --priority 2\n1644\tbf claim --any --assignee \"multi-worker\" --json --workspace /tmp/ws-a --workspace /tmp/ws-b\n1645\t# Should get ws-b's \"ws-a high\" (priority 0)\n1646\t```\n1647\t\n1648\t---\n1649\t\n1650\t## Implementation Order\n1651\t\n1652\t| Phase | Description | Estimated Effort |\n1653\t|-------|-------------|-----------------|\n1654\t| 1 | Core library (model, JSONL read/write, config, ID gen) | Foundation |\n1655\t| 2 | SQLite cache layer (schema, storage, sync, doctor) | Medium |\n1656\t| 3 | CLI commands (all br-compatible commands) | Medium |\n1657\t| 4 | Concurrent claiming (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, impact scoring, stale reclamation, multi-workspace) | Medium |\n1658\t| 4B | Extended features (log rotation, batch ops, annotations, operation history, secret scanning, critical path, velocity scoring) | Medium |\n1659\t| 5 | NEEDLE integration (pluck.sh update, backward compat) | Small |\n1660\t| 6 | Build & deploy (CI, binary) | Small |\n1661\t| 7 | Upstream robustness parity: auto-flush + dirty tracking, doctor safety stack, NULL hardening, anomaly verdicts, update/batch/JSON-contract gaps, derived blocked, multi-box concurrency | Medium-Large |\n1662\t\n1663\tPhases 1-3 produce a fully functional standalone `bf` that replaces `br`. Phase 4 adds atomic claiming for fleet operations. Phase 4B adds extended features that make bf more powerful than br. Phases 5-6 integrate and deploy. Phase 7 (added 2026-07-21) back-ports the robustness behaviors upstream `beads_rust` developed after the fork — P0 items first (7.1-7.3), then P1 (7.4-7.7), then the architectural/multi-box P2 items (7.8-7.9).\n1664\t\n1665\t---\n1666\t\n1667\t## Key Design Decisions\n1668\t\n1669\t1. **SQLite-primary, JSONL as git artifact**: SQLite is the live database — all reads and writes go through it. JSONL is exported on `bf sync` for git commit, providing backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. This matches how bd and br work, but with rusqlite (no corruption) and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for atomic claim (no race condition).\n1670\t\n1671\t2. **rusqlite, not FrankenSQLite**: We already proved in the beads_rust fork that FrankenSQLite has corruption issues. Start clean with rusqlite.\n1672\t\n1673\t3. **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for atomic claim**: The read-score-update sequence runs in a single SQLite write transaction. No flock, no streaming rewrite, no temp files. SQLite's own locking serializes concurrent claims correctly.\n1674\t\n1675\t4. **No automatic git commits**: Match br's explicit, non-invasive philosophy. Users run `bf sync` when they want to commit JSONL changes.\n1676\t\n1677\t5. **Cattle, not pets**: Workers are disposable fleet units with no identity, no memory, and no conversation. Claims are atomic SQL dequeues from a priority queue, not negotiations.\n1678\t\n1679\t6. **Stale reclamation as a side effect of claiming**: The first statement in every `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` claim transaction resets expired `in_progress` beads. No separate heartbeat system, no background process.\n1680\t\n1681\t7. **Server as future optimization, not v1**: A persistent in-memory server would reduce per-claim latency from ~2ms to ~0.1ms by eliminating SQLite file I/O. Premature for current scale — can be added transparently later.\n1682\t\n1683\t8. **Rotation keeps JSONL artifact lean**: Closed beads older than `rotate_age_days` are exported to archive files (`issues.jsonl.1`, etc.) rather than the active `issues.jsonl`. Keeps the committed artifact small and git diffs readable.\n1684\t\n1685\t9. **Annotations as extension mechanism**: Arbitrary `BTreeMap<String, String>` on beads lets external tools (NEEDLE, custom scripts) store structured metadata without schema changes. Stored in a separate `bead_annotations` table — never as a column on `issues` — because br's `issues_column_order_matches()` triggers `rebuild_issues_table()` on any column count mismatch, silently destroying any extra column on every br open. br never reads or writes `bead_annotations`, so annotation data survives any br operation unchanged.\n1686\t\n1687\t10. **Events table for history**: Every mutation records an event row. `bf log` queries the events table — O(1) by issue ID. Long-term history via git log on `issues.jsonl`.\n1688\t\n1689\t11. **Secret scanning before write**: Built-in regex-based secret detection prevents credentials from entering SQLite or the JSONL export. Configurable patterns, git pre-commit hook integration.\n1690\t\n1691\t12. **`.beads/` is committed to git**: `issues.jsonl` + config are version-controlled. `beads.db` is gitignored (binary, rebuilt from JSONL on `bf sync --import`). Secret scanning protects the exported JSONL.\n1692\t\n1693\t13. **Critical path drives claim priority, not just listed priority**: Listed priority is a human signal, but it decays as the project evolves and humans stop curating it. Critical path float is computed from the live dependency graph and is always current. A priority-3 bead on the critical path outranks a priority-0 bead with float=5 — the fleet naturally works on what matters most without human recuration.\n1694\t\n1695\t14. **Worker composition is first-class metadata**: `--model`, `--harness`, `--harness-version` on `bf claim` record what kind of agent did the work. This transforms the events table from a bare audit log into a performance dataset: which model+harness combinations close which task types fastest. The fleet becomes self-optimizing — velocity data informs which workers to dispatch to which workspace, without any external ML pipeline.\n1696\t\n1697\t15. **Upstream br is a tracked ideas source, ported one-way as behaviors, never merged as code** (2026-07-21): beads_rust keeps solving dual-store robustness problems bf also has — credit where due, Emanuel keeps finding improvements on top of what already exists. The codebases are architecturally divergent and upstream accepts no PRs (their agents integrate from filed issues), so the flow is: study upstream behavior → spec it against bf's architecture in this plan (Phase 7) → implement natively with attribution. Never vendor upstream code, never chase their product surface (see Phase 7 Non-goals), and periodically re-scan their tracker/source for new robustness work worth porting.\n1698\t\n1699\t---\n1700\t\n1701\t## Architecture Decision Records\n1702\t\n1703\t### ADR-1: Periodic `.beads/` git checkpoint timer (2026-07-20)\n1704\t\n1705\t**Status:** Accepted & implemented — `bf-checkpoint.{sh,service,timer}` ship in `deploy/` (Debian/Ubuntu) and `systemd/` (NixOS); `CheckpointConfig` parses the block in `src/config.rs`. Parent bead: `bf-48pw0`.\n1706\t\n1707\t**Context.** bead-forge is a dual-store system: SQLite (`beads.db`) is the live store and `issues.jsonl` is the git-tracked checkpoint (see Core Principle #2 and §2.7). Historically, mutations did not auto-flush, so a workspace under active NEEDLE work could accumulate **db-only** beads never captured in git — losing the box meant losing work, and shared workspaces (many agents in one tree) had no coherent, low-noise way to land periodic snapshots. Phase 7.1's `sync.auto_flush` (default on) closes the per-mutation gap, but a periodic out-of-band safety net is still wanted so that even a workspace whose agents exit ungracefully still gets its state committed to git.\n1708\t\n1709\t**Decision.** A dedicated systemd timer (`bf-checkpoint.timer` → `bf-checkpoint.service` → `bf-checkpoint.sh`) periodically flushes SQLite → JSONL via `bf sync --flush-only` and, if `.beads/issues.jsonl` changed, stages **only** that file and commits it as `chore(beads): auto-checkpoint <UTC>`. It runs strictly out-of-band — driven by the timer, never by any `bf` command. New rollouts default to **`checkpoint.enabled: false`**; a maintainer must opt each workspace in. `git push` is off by default.\n1710\t\n1711\t**Consequences.**\n1712\t\n1713\t- **Out-of-band only.** `src/claim.rs` and the claim/close hot path are never touched — no git or flush work on the latency-critical dequeue path. Checkpointing cannot regress claim latency or contend with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` write transactions on the hot path.\n1714\t- **Exactly one committed path.** Only `.beads/issues.jsonl` is ever staged. `beads.db` is never staged — it is gitignored and rebuilt from JSONL via `bf sync --import`.\n1715\t- **Safe by default / opt-in.** A freshly deployed timer is inert: `bf-checkpoint.sh` prints `checkpoint disabled` and exits 0 until `checkpoint.enabled: true`. Cadence is governed by `checkpoint.interval_minutes` via a per-workspace self-throttle state file, not by how often the timer fires.\n1716\t- **Distinguishable commits.** A fixed identity (`jedarden <github@jedarden.com>`) and the `chore(beads): auto-checkpoint` prefix keep machine checkpoints separable from human commits.\n1717\t- **Push stays opt-in.** Enabled persistently by `checkpoint.push: true` or one-shot by the script's `--push` flag. The unit's `ExecStart` must never carry `--push`, which would force-push on every timer fire.\n1718\t\n1719\t**Config block** (`.beads/config.yaml`):\n1720\t\n1721\t```yaml\n1722\tcheckpoint:\n1723\t  enabled: false           # master switch; NEW ROLLOUTS STAY DISABLED until a maintainer opts in\n1724\t  interval_minutes: 60     # min gap between commits (self-throttle), default 60\n1725\t  push: false              # git push after each commit, default false\n1726\t```\n1727\t\n1728\t---\n1729\t\n1730\t## Alternative Approaches Considered\n1731\t\n1732\t### In-Memory Server (deferred)\n1733\t\n1734\tThe plan originally included a coordination server: persistent process, Unix socket protocol, `Arc<Mutex<ServerState>>`, in-memory BTreeMap priority queues, heartbeat-based stale detection. This was deferred to a future optimization because SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` delivers sufficient throughput at current scale.\n1735\t\n1736\tThe server would reduce per-claim latency from ~2ms (SQLite transaction) to ~0.1ms (memory pop). This matters only if fleets exceed 50 workers or claim frequency exceeds ~500/sec — neither is on the horizon. The server can be added transparently: `bf claim` detects the server socket, delegates if present, falls back to SQLite if not.\n1737\t\n1738\t### MCP Agent Mail (Dicklesworthstone/mcp_agent_mail_rust)\n1739\t\n1740\tJeffrey Emanuel's companion system for inter-agent coordination. A Rust MCP server with 36 tools, 33 resources, Git-backed archive, SQLite indexing, HTTP/TUI/Robot surfaces.\n1741\t\n1742\t**Architecture**: Agents register identities, claim file reservations with TTL, exchange threaded messages, negotiate work assignments via acknowledgements. Coordination happens through conversation — \"I'm taking src/auth/**, can you work on tests/?\"\n1743\t\n1744\t**Why it doesn't fit bead-forge**: Agent Mail is built for the **pets** model — named, persistent agents that maintain identity across sessions, negotiate via messaging, and coordinate through conversation. NEEDLE uses the **cattle** model — disposable workers that are interchangeable, stateless, and need atomic dequeue without any conversation.\n1745\t\n1746\t| Aspect | Agent Mail (Pets) | bead-forge (Cattle) |\n1747\t|--------|-------------------|---------------------|\n1748\t| Agent identity | Registered, named, persistent | Anonymous, stateless, disposable |\n1749\t| Work assignment | Negotiation, messaging, agreement | Atomic SQL dequeue (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) |\n1750\t| Coordination mechanism | Threaded messages, acknowledgements | Kernel-provided mutual exclusion |\n1751\t| File/workspace ownership | Advisory file reservations | None — beads are the unit of work |\n1752\t| Communication pattern | Multi-turn conversation | Single CLI invocation |\n1753\t| Failure mode | Agent re-joins conversation | Agent dies, claim TTL expires, bead reopens |\n1754\t| Agent count | Small (3-5 named agents) | Large fleet (11-20+ disposable workers) |\n1755\t\n1756\t**What to borrow from Agent Mail**:\n1757\t- **TTL-based claim expiration**: Agent Mail uses TTL on file reservations. bead-forge applies the same concept — claims older than `claim_ttl` are reclaimed to `open` on the next claim invocation.\n1758\t\n1759\t**What to explicitly reject**:\n1760\t- **Agent identities**: Workers don't register or maintain identity. The `--assignee` field is for logging, not identity.\n1761\t- **Messaging/threading**: Workers don't send messages to each other. The only communication is claim/close through the JSONL file.\n1762\t- **File reservations**: Workers operate on entire beads, not file-level reservations.\n1763\t- **MCP layer**: bead-forge is a CLI. No stdio-based MCP protocol.\n1764\t- **Advisory locks**: Claims are enforced by `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, not advisory. Once claimed (inside the transaction), no other worker sees that bead as open.\n1765\t\n1766\t### BeadHub (juanre/beadhub)\n1767\t\n1768\tA coordination server for AI agent teams built on top of Steve Yegge's Dolt-based `bd`. The `bdh` CLI wraps `bd` and adds work claiming, file reservation, presence awareness, and inter-agent messaging. Includes a web dashboard.\n1769\t\n1770\t**Why it doesn't fit**: Tied to Dolt-based `bd` architecture (not JSONL). bead-forge needs JSONL+SQLite compatibility with br, not Dolt compatibility with bd. However, the coordination server concept validates that this problem is real and worth solving.\n1771\t\n1772\t### Beads Viewer (Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer)\n1773\t\n1774\tGraph-aware TUI with PageRank-based prioritization, critical path analysis, and kanban board view.\n1775\t\n1776\t**Why it doesn't fit**: Read-only visualization tool. Cannot perform writes (claiming, status changes). The PageRank and critical path concepts are interesting for future prioritization but don't solve the concurrency problem.\n1777\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c22178ff-4dec-4f61-91f5-63794ea70001","uuid":"9e53a55f-ffc3-4627-90b7-8b1cd9cb492b","timestamp":"2026-07-23T19:18:35.135Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/coding/bead-forge/docs/plan/plan.md","content":"# bead-forge Implementation Plan\n\n> **User-facing documentation:** [`../README.md`](../README.md) — overview, command reference, NEEDLE integration guide, and hero image.\n\n## Overview\n\n**bead-forge** (`bf`) is a Rust binary that replaces `br` (beads_rust). SQLite is the live database — all reads and writes go through it. `issues.jsonl` is a git-synced artifact exported on demand: one entry per bead, committed to the repo for backup, sharing, and recovery. Concurrent claiming is handled by SQLite's `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction — no server, no daemon, no flock required.\n\n## Core Principles\n\n1. **SQLite is the live store** — all mutations are SQL writes; reads are SQL queries. Fast, concurrent-read, serialized-write via WAL mode.\n2. **JSONL is the git artifact** — exported on `bf sync`, committed to git, one entry per bead. Used for backup, cross-machine sharing, and recovery. ~~Never written during normal operation.~~ *(Amended 2026-07-21, Phase 7.1: with `sync.auto_flush` — default on — every successful mutation incrementally exports the changed beads to JSONL, so the artifact tracks the live store instead of trailing it. `bf sync --flush-only` remains the explicit checkpoint and the recovery path when auto-flush fails. Read-only commands still never write.)*\n3. **Drop-in CLI** — all `br` commands work under `bf` with the same flags and output formats\n4. **`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for atomic claim** — the read-score-update sequence runs inside a single SQLite write transaction, eliminating the race condition `br` has without requiring flock or a daemon\n\n---\n\n## Phase 1: Core Library — Data Model & JSONL Import/Export\n\n### 1.1 Data Model (`src/model.rs`)\n\nPort the exact `Issue`, `Status`, `Priority`, `IssueType`, `Dependency`, `DependencyType`, `Comment`, and `Event` structs from beads_rust with identical Serde attributes. This is the wire format — every field, every `skip_serializing_if`, every rename must match.\n\nKey structs and their JSONL serialization:\n\n```\nStatus:       open | in_progress | blocked | deferred | draft | closed | tombstone | pinned | Custom(String)\nPriority:     transparent i32 (0=Critical, 4=Backlog)\nIssueType:    task | bug | feature | epic | chore | docs | question | Custom(String)\nDependency:   { issue_id, depends_on_id, type (renamed from dep_type), created_at, created_by?, metadata?, thread_id? }\nComment:      { id: i64, issue_id, author, text (renamed from body), created_at }\nEvent:        { id: i64, issue_id, event_type, actor, old_value?, new_value?, comment?, created_at }\n```\n\nIssue fields (alphabetical by JSON key):\n```\nid, title, description?, design?, acceptance_criteria?, notes?,\nstatus, priority, issue_type, assignee?, owner?, estimated_minutes?,\ncreated_at, created_by?, updated_at, closed_at?, close_reason?,\nclosed_by_session?, due_at?, defer_until?, external_ref?,\nsource_system?, source_repo, deleted_at?, deleted_by?, delete_reason?,\noriginal_type?, compaction_level (default 0), compacted_at?,\ncompacted_at_commit?, original_size?, sender?, ephemeral (default false),\npinned (default false), is_template (default false),\nlabels: Vec<String>, dependencies: Vec<Dependency>, comments: Vec<Comment>\n```\n\n### 1.2 JSONL Import (`src/jsonl.rs`)\n\nJSONL is read only during `bf sync --import` (pulling state from git) and `bf doctor --repair` (rebuilding SQLite from the artifact). Never read during normal CLI operation.\n\n```rust\nfn import_jsonl(jsonl_path: &Path, storage: &Storage) -> Result<ImportResult> {\n    let file = File::open(jsonl_path)?;\n    let reader = BufReader::new(file);\n    storage.with_write_transaction(|tx| {\n        for line in reader.lines() {\n            let issue: Issue = serde_json::from_str(&line?)?;\n            tx.upsert_issue(&issue)?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    })\n}\n```\n\nFunctions:\n- `import_jsonl(path, storage)` — bulk upsert from JSONL into SQLite\n- `stream_issues(path) -> impl Iterator<Item = Result<Issue>>` — lazy line iterator (used by import and doctor)\n\n### 1.3 JSONL Export (`src/jsonl.rs`)\n\nJSONL is written only during `bf sync --flush` (preparing the git artifact). Exports current bead state from SQLite, one entry per bead, sorted by ID for stable diffs. Atomic temp+rename.\n\n```rust\nfn export_jsonl(jsonl_path: &Path, storage: &Storage) -> Result<ExportResult> {\n    let issues = storage.list_all_issues()?;  // sorted by ID\n    let temp_path = jsonl_path.with_extension(\"jsonl.tmp\");\n    let mut writer = BufWriter::new(File::create_new(&temp_path)?);\n    for issue in &issues {\n        serde_json::to_writer(&mut writer, issue)?;\n        writer.write_all(b\"\\n\")?;\n    }\n    writer.flush()?;\n    drop(writer);\n    fs::rename(&temp_path, jsonl_path)?;\n    Ok(ExportResult { count: issues.len() })\n}\n```\n\nFunctions:\n- `export_jsonl(path, storage)` — dump all beads from SQLite to JSONL (atomic)\n- `export_jsonl_dirty(path, storage)` — export only dirty beads (incremental, faster for large workspaces)\n\n### 1.4 Config (`src/config.rs`)\n\nParse `.beads/config.yaml` with the same fields br uses:\n\n```yaml\nissue_prefixes: [bd, fg]\ndefault_priority: 2\ndefault_type: task\nscoring:\n  priority_weight: 0.4\n  blockers_weight: 0.3\n  age_weight: 0.2\n  labels_weight: 0.1\n  max_age_hours: 20\n  max_blockers: 3\n# bead-forge additions (additive, br ignores these)\nclaim_ttl_minutes: 30\n```\n\nParse `.beads/metadata.json`:\n```json\n{ \"database\": \"beads.db\", \"jsonl_export\": \"issues.jsonl\" }\n```\n\n### 1.5 ID Generation (`src/id.rs`)\n\nPort br's ID scheme: `<prefix>-<hash>` where hash is base36 lowercase. Use the birthday-problem adaptive length (3-8 chars). Read `issue_prefixes` from config (first entry is the default prefix).\n\n```rust\nfn generate_id(prefix: &str, existing_count: usize) -> String {\n    let len = optimal_hash_length(existing_count);\n    let random_bytes = rand::random::<[u8; 16]>();\n    let hash = sha256(&random_bytes);\n    base36_encode(&hash[..len])\n    format!(\"{}-{}\", prefix, hash)\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Phase 2: SQLite Primary Store\n\n### 2.1 Schema Application (`src/storage/schema.rs`)\n\nApply the exact same `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` DDL from br's `SCHEMA_SQL`. Tables:\n\n| Table | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| `issues` | All 35 columns, same types, defaults, CHECK constraints |\n| `dependencies` | (issue_id, depends_on_id) PK, type, metadata, thread_id |\n| `labels` | (issue_id, label) PK |\n| `comments` | AUTOINCREMENT id, issue_id, author, text, created_at |\n| `events` | AUTOINCREMENT id, issue_id, event_type, actor, old/new/comment |\n| `config` | key-value |\n| `metadata` | key-value |\n| `dirty_issues` | Track which issues need JSONL export |\n| `export_hashes` | Incremental export tracking |\n| `blocked_issues_cache` | Materialized view of blocked issues |\n| `child_counters` | Hierarchical IDs (bd-abc.1, bd-abc.2) |\n| `recovery_sessions` | Anomaly/recovery audit trail |\n| `anomaly_audit` | Recovery event tracking |\n| `bead_annotations` | bf-only: arbitrary key-value metadata per bead; separate table so br's `rebuild_issues_table()` never touches it |\n\nAll indexes from br must be created identically, including the critical `idx_issues_ready` composite partial index.\n\n### 2.2 Storage Engine (`src/storage/sqlite.rs`)\n\nUse `rusqlite` (not FrankenSQLite) bundled with system SQLite. Apply WAL mode, foreign keys, busy_timeout=30s, cache_size=-8000, synchronous=NORMAL.\n\nAll mutations go through here. JSONL is never touched during normal operation.\n\nFunctions:\n- `open(path: &Path) -> Result<Storage>` — open/create DB, apply schema\n- `get_issue(id: &str) -> Result<Option<Issue>>` — point lookup by ID\n- `list_issues(filter: IssueFilter) -> Result<Vec<Issue>>` — filtered query with WHERE clauses\n- `list_all_issues() -> Result<Vec<Issue>>` — full table scan sorted by ID (for JSONL export)\n- `create_issue(issue: &Issue) -> Result<()>` — INSERT\n- `update_issue(id: &str, changes: IssueChanges) -> Result<()>` — UPDATE + mark dirty\n- `close_issue(id: &str, reason: &str) -> Result<()>` — status transition + mark dirty\n- `with_write_transaction(f) -> Result<T>` — execute closure in a write transaction\n- `with_immediate_transaction(f) -> Result<T>` — `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` with retry (see §2.5) — acquires write lock before any reads (used by claim)\n- `rebuild_blocked_cache() -> Result<()>` — recalculate blocked issues materialized view\n\n### 2.3 Sync Protocol (`src/sync.rs`)\n\nPort br's sync semantics:\n\n**Flush (SQLite → JSONL, for git)**:\n1. Call `export_jsonl_dirty` — query dirty bead IDs, export full current state of each from SQLite\n2. Atomic temp+rename over `issues.jsonl`\n3. Clear `dirty_issues`, update `export_hashes`\n\nFor `bf sync` (full flush): call `export_jsonl` — dump all beads sorted by ID, unconditionally.\n\n**Import (JSONL → SQLite, from git pull)**:\n1. Stream `issues.jsonl` line by line\n2. Compare each with SQLite state using `content_hash`\n3. INSERT new, UPDATE changed, SKIP unchanged\n4. Handle collisions (same ID, different content) with deterministic resolution\n\n### 2.5 Concurrent Write Safety (`src/storage/sqlite.rs`)\n\nSQLite WAL mode serializes concurrent writers through a single write lock — they queue, not corrupt. `SQLITE_BUSY` is returned when a writer cannot acquire the lock within `busy_timeout`. With claim latency of ~1-2ms and a 20-worker fleet, the entire queue clears in ~20-40ms, so `SQLITE_BUSY` should never occur in normal operation. However, a retry wrapper is the cheap safety net that makes this a guarantee rather than an assumption:\n\n```rust\nconst MAX_RETRIES: u32 = 5;\nconst RETRY_BASE_MS: u64 = 50;\n\nfn with_immediate_transaction<T>(\n    conn: &Connection,\n    f: impl Fn(&Transaction) -> Result<T>,\n) -> Result<T> {\n    let mut attempt = 0;\n    loop {\n        match conn.execute(\"BEGIN IMMEDIATE\", []) {\n            Ok(_) => {\n                let tx = conn.unchecked_transaction()?;\n                return match f(&tx) {\n                    Ok(val) => { tx.commit()?; Ok(val) }\n                    Err(e) => { let _ = tx.rollback(); Err(e) }\n                };\n            }\n            Err(e) if is_busy_error(&e) && attempt < MAX_RETRIES => {\n                attempt += 1;\n                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(RETRY_BASE_MS * attempt as u64));\n                continue;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn is_busy_error(e: &rusqlite::Error) -> bool {\n    matches!(\n        e,\n        rusqlite::Error::SqliteFailure(\n            rusqlite::ffi::Error { code: rusqlite::ErrorCode::DatabaseBusy, .. },\n            _\n        )\n    )\n}\n```\n\n**Why this is sufficient and not a workaround**: `SQLITE_BUSY` with WAL mode is not data corruption — it is a clean \"lock unavailable, try again\" signal. The database is fully consistent when this occurs. The retry converts a transient contention spike (e.g., 20 workers all starting within the same millisecond) into a short wait rather than a user-visible error.\n\n**All write operations** (`claim`, `create`, `update`, `close`, `batch`) use `with_immediate_transaction`. Read-only operations (`list`, `show`, `ready`) use a plain `BEGIN DEFERRED` transaction and are never affected by write contention.\n\n### 2.7 Doctor/Repair (`src/doctor.rs`)\n\n- `doctor --repair`: Delete `beads.db`, reimport from JSONL\n- `doctor --check`: Validate JSONL line integrity, check SQLite <-> JSONL consistency\n- `doctor --repair --flush-first`: Flush unflushed beads to JSONL before repairing (protects against data loss)\n- `doctor --repair --force`: Force repair even with unflushed beads (WARNING: unflushed beads are lost)\n- **Flush-before-repair rule**: Always run `bf sync --flush-only` before `bf doctor --repair` to protect against losing unflushed beads\n- Recovery from corruption: JSONL export is the authoritative checkpoint for recovery — `beads.db` can be rebuilt from it at any time\n\n**CRITICAL DATA AUTHORITY NOTE**: bead-forge inverts the authority model from upstream beads/br:\n\n| Tool | Source of truth | Checkpoint role |\n|------|----------------|-----------------|\n| beads / br | JSONL (`issues.jsonl`) | SQLite is read-cache |\n| bead-forge | SQLite (`beads.db`) | JSONL is git-tracked checkpoint |\n\nThis inversion is necessary for atomic multi-worker operations. **Beads created or modified since the last `bf sync --flush-only` exist only in SQLite**. Running `bf doctor --repair` without flushing first destroys these unflushed beads.\n\n**Historical context**: On 2026-06-10, seven independent agents across seven workspaces (ARMOR, NEEDLE, AgentScribe, kalshi-weather, jedarden.com, vibe-coding-discovery, face/pose/sun repos) each lost their entire first batch of freshly created beads by running `doctor --repair` after bulk creates. Four db-only beads in ARMOR (bf-4rm7/5zxa/tojg/tr44) were permanently lost. This fix implements the flush-before-repair protection.\n\n---\n\n## Phase 3: CLI Commands\n\n### 3.1 Command Structure (`src/cli/`)\n\nUse `clap` with derive macros. Binary name: `bf`. Subcommands mirror br exactly.\n\n```\nbf create    --title \"...\" --type <type> --priority <N> [--description \"...\"] [--label ...]\nbf list      [--status <s>] [--type <t>] [--assignee <a>] [--limit N] [--format json|text|toon]\nbf show      <id>\nbf update    <id> [--status <s>] [--assignee <a>] [--priority <N>] [--title \"...\"] ...\nbf close     <id> [--reason \"...\"]\nbf reopen    <id>\nbf delete    <id>\nbf ready         [--limit N]                     #
